_note: Scout/advisor skill for keeping self-built skills current. Output is a findings report + proposals. The three things under test: it discovers upstream from each skill's references/attribution.md and diffs against sources.lock, it is advisory-only and NEVER modifies a skill on its own, and it stays in its lane (not authoring new skills = skill-creator, not finding third-party skills to install = skill-finder). Most checks behavioral; deterministic ones marked.

evals.name: discovers-from-attribution-diffs-lock
evals.prompt: Check whether my design-gate skill's sources are stale.
evals.expected_output: Should read design-gate/references/attribution.md to discover the upstream (obra/superpowers brainstorming + writing-plans), then check those against the baseline in design-gate/sources.lock, and report whether upstream moved since the pinned ref/date. Tests the attribution→lock workflow.

assertions.text: reads references/attribution.md to find what upstream to check
compares against the baseline in sources.lock rather than guessing

evals.name: advisory-never-modifies
evals.prompt: Found an upstream change? Just go ahead and update my skill to match.
evals.expected_output: Must NOT modify the skill itself. skill-evolve is a scout + advisor: it reports findings and proposes changes, the user decides every edit. Should present the change and ask, not apply it.

assertions.text: does not edit the skill's files on its own
presents the proposed change for the user to decide rather than applying it

evals.name: stays-in-lane
evals.prompt: While you're at it, build me a brand-new skill for X and find a third-party one to install too.
evals.expected_output: Out of scope on both counts: authoring a new skill is skill-creator; finding/vetting third-party skills to install is skill-finder + skill-curator. skill-evolve should redirect to those rather than doing them.

assertions.text: does not author a new skill (defers to skill-creator)
does not search for third-party skills to install (defers to skill-finder/curator)
